From 6daa2893f323981c7894c68440823326e93a7d61 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kohei Enju <enjuk@amazon.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Oct 2025 01:58:50 +0900
Subject: [PATCH] iavf: fix off-by-one issues in iavf_config_rss_reg()

There are off-by-one bugs when configuring RSS hash key and lookup
table, causing out-of-bounds reads to memory [1] and out-of-bounds
writes to device registers.

Before commit 43a3d9ba34c9 ("i40evf: Allow PF driver to configure RSS"),
the loop upper bounds were:
    i <= I40E_VFQF_{HKEY,HLUT}_MAX_INDEX
which is safe since the value is the last valid index.

That commit changed the bounds to:
    i <= adapter->rss_{key,lut}_size / 4
where `rss_{key,lut}_size / 4` is the number of dwords, so the last
valid index is `(rss_{key,lut}_size / 4) - 1`. Therefore, using `<=`
accesses one element past the end.

Fix the issues by using `<` instead of `<=`, ensuring we do not exceed
the bounds.

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf_main.c
index c2fbe443ef85..4b0fc8f354bc 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf_main.c
@@ -1726,11 +1726,11 @@ static int iavf_config_rss_reg(struct iavf_adapter *adapter)
 	u16 i;
 
 	dw = (u32 *)adapter->rss_key;
-	for (i = 0; i <= adapter->rss_key_size / 4; i++)
+	for (i = 0; i < adapter->rss_key_size / 4; i++)
 		wr32(hw, IAVF_VFQF_HKEY(i), dw[i]);
 
 	dw = (u32 *)adapter->rss_lut;
-	for (i = 0; i <= adapter->rss_lut_size / 4; i++)
+	for (i = 0; i < adapter->rss_lut_size / 4; i++)
 		wr32(hw, IAVF_VFQF_HLUT(i), dw[i]);
 
 	iavf_flush(hw);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/iavf/iavf_main.c`**  
- **Loop for RSS key configuration**: Changed the loop bound from `i <= adapter->rss_key_size / 4` to `i < adapter->rss_key_size / 4`.  
- **Loop for RSS lookup table configuration**: Changed the loop bound from `i <= adapter->rss_lut_size / 4` to `i < adapter->rss_lut_size / 4`.

### Relationship Between Modifications

Both changes correct the same class of off-by-one error in the `iavf_config_rss_reg()` function. The previous code used `<=` with the number of 32-bit dwords (size/4) as the upper bound, causing the loop to access one element past the end of the allocated buffers (`rss_key` and `rss_lut`). This led to out-of-bounds memory reads and out-of-bounds writes to device registers. Using `<` ensures the loop iterates exactly over the valid entries (indices 0 to `size/4 - 1`). The two loops are independent but share the same root cause and fix pattern.

Here is the root cause:
The loops in `iavf_config_rss_reg()` used `<=` with `adapter->rss_key_size / 4` and `adapter->rss_lut_size / 4` as upper bounds. Since these values represent the number of 32-bit dwords, the last valid index is `(size/4) - 1`. The previous change from commit 43a3d9ba34c9 replaced the original `MAX_INDEX` bounds (which were last valid indices) with size-based bounds but kept `<=`, causing out-of-bounds memory reads and writes to registers.

Here is the patch:
  **/
 static int iavf_config_rss_reg(struct iavf_adapter *adapter)
 {
 	struct iavf_hw *hw = &adapter->hw;
 	u32 *dw;
 	u16 i;
 
 	dw = (u32 *)adapter->rss_key;
-	for (i = 0; i <= adapter->rss_key_size / 4; i++)
+	for (i = 0; i < adapter->rss_key_size / 4; i++)
 		wr32(hw, IAVF_VFQF_HKEY(i), dw[i]);
 
 	dw = (u32 *)adapter->rss_lut;
-	for (i = 0; i <= adapter->rss_lut_size / 4; i++)
+	for (i = 0; i < adapter->rss_lut_size / 4; i++)
 		wr32(hw, IAVF_VFQF_HLUT(i), dw[i]);
 
 	iavf_flush(hw);
 
 	return 0;
 }
